18:05 Local Time, 12:35 GMT | Stumps, Day 2: We lost the first one and a half sessions today with rain playing hide and seek. 43 overs were bowled and India added 172 runs in the process. Sri Lanka bowled a lot better, with their spinners being consistent with their lengths and the wickets column is a testament to that. Debutant Keshara Nuwantha was trusted with the second new ball and he removed Pant and KL Rahul. Devdutt Padikkal continued from where he left yesterday, crossed 150 before getting out stumped for 167 off Prabath.

Jadeja became Keshara's third victim after the Tea break. That brought Dhruv Jurel and Manav Suthar together and the duo forged a 55-run stand to take India's total over 400. Jurel got a reprieve on 29 and he went on to notch up a fifty before a stunning catch from DDS ended his knock. Siraj tried to be aggressive and perished to Asitha and Suthar fell to Jayasuriya off the very next ball. India continued to bat and the final pair survived the last 17 balls of the day to take their team's total to 460. India are in a commanding position in this Test. Will they continue to bat or declare overnight? Batting could get tougher as this Test progresses. So, the Sri Lankans have an uphill task to stage a comeback in this game. Tune in tomorrow to find out how the action pans out. And, let's hope that the weather stays clear.

Devdutt Padikkal (1/3): (Your thoughts on the first Test hundred, must be very special!) Yeah, definitely. I've dreamt of this moment. For the last two years, I've been working really hard to try and make sure that when I get that opportunity, I can do something special like this, and I'm really happy to do that. (On his aggressive intent vs spin early on and decisive footwork) Yeah, I think we have discussed that at length, especially when you're playing spin, it's important that you have certain plans in your head. You cannot go out there and expect to react all the time. It's important that we have a couple of shots in your head that you want to play as soon as you go out there, so that you can put some pressure on the bowler as well. So, I think over the last year or so, we have really worked on trying to find ways in our own strengths that you can really implement to make sure that you put pressure back.

Padikkal (3/3): (Surface gripping a little bit more on day two?) Not a whole lot more. I think it will take probably another couple of sessions for that to really start breaking up. But we know that in Galle, especially, it tends to quicken up pretty fast on the third and fourth day. So we are expecting that to happen again. Hopefully, it will help our bowlers as well. (Are you the kind that celebrates hard after a big performance? Not really (smiles). I think I'm tired, so I'm just going to go back to bed now.

09:00 Local Time, 03:30 GMT: Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of Day 3 of the Galle Test. While many around the world are battling the dreaded Monday blues, our biggest concern here is a little different: will we get clear blue skies throughout the day? The first two days were heavily interrupted by rain, with Day 2 seeing more disruption as almost a session and a half was lost before the start of play. We now head into Day 3 hoping the rain stays away, but the forecast isn't particularly encouraging. Rain was predicted across all five days of the Test, with scattered thunderstorms also expected today.

What transpired on Day 2? Only 43 overs were possible, with India adding 172 runs but losing seven wickets in the process. The Sri Lankan spinners bowled with much better control, and debutant Keshara Nuwantha struck twice in quick succession, dismissing Rishabh Pant and KL Rahul with the second new ball. Devdutt Padikkal continued his fine knock, scoring 167 before being stumped off Prabath Jayasuriya. Dhruv Jurel also chipped in with a fifty, while the lower order made decent contributions as India finished the day on 460/9. The surface is likely to deteriorate as the day progresses, and the Indian spinners should enjoy bowling on it. There’s no official word yet, but it wouldn’t be a surprise if India have declared overnight and decide to put Sri Lanka in straightaway today.

Good news to start with: we have bright skies and plenty of sunshine in Galle. Hopefully, the weather stays kind to us and we get a full day of uninterrupted action. We can only hope, and there’s certainly no harm in that.

We can see the Indian team in a huddle, with head coach Gautam Gambhir doing the talking. It’s still bright and sunny in Galle. India have 460 runs on the board with one wicket in hand, but it remains to be seen whether they come out to bat or declare and ask Sri Lanka to start the day. We will find out shortly, with play set to begin at 9:45 AM.
Doesn’t look like there’s going to be a declaration. We can see Kuldeep Yadav and Prasidh Krishna padded up, suggesting India will come out to bat.
